items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: No record executive could have told Louis Armstrong to go in and record the Hot Fives.

ctx.x: That’s a great thought I think.

I mean I really trust jazz so much. Despite the challenges that the musicians have faced for a hundred years now, they have been able to really devote themselves to creating some incredible art that nobody could have made. Nobody except the artists themselves could have made it. No record executive could have told Louis Armstrong to go in and record the Hot Fives. You know? They just couldn’t have imagined it. And I think that it’s a lot easier for a record executive or producer to say to a country artist who is…

between what the average listener, the common American, is ready to accept as music, and what the very sophisticated and very creative artist in sound is able to realize. There is so much gap between that that I really don’t see that it’s going to connect in an easy way. What with face paint? Or with an advertising campaign? It wouldn’t hurt. It wouldn’t hurt to demystify some of the stuff that goes into jazz, it would help. And I think jazz education is doing a good job with that. Not just the IAJE conferences…
